name: Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Ulna

criteria.description: Radiographic evidence of nonunion or pseudoarthrosis of the ulna present at birth or early infancy
Visible deformity or angulation of the ulna with abnormal mobility at the pseudoarthrosis site
No history of trauma or fracture explaining the nonunion
Presence or absence of neurofibromatosis type 1 features (may be associated but not required)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radiographic nonunion of the ulna at birth or early infancy with clinical deformity and absence of trauma history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may be considered if neurofibromatosis is suspected.

pathognomonic.notes: Definitive feature characterized by failure of normal bone continuity
searchTerms: birth defect causing ulna bone not to join
ulna bone never fusing since birth

pathognomonic.notes: Deformity typically present at birth or early infancy
searchTerms: visible bending of the ulna bone

common.symptomName: Abnormal mobility at the pseudoarthrosis site
common.notes: Movement at the site of nonunion causing functional impairment
searchTerms: excessive motion where bone should be solid

common.notes: Relative shortening of the affected forearm compared to contralateral side

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion of the elbow joint
common.notes: Restriction due to deformity or instability

common.symptomName: Mild pain or discomfort localized to the forearm
common.notes: Usually intermittent and related to mechanical stress

occasional.notes: May occur secondary to ulna deformity
searchTerms: radial bone out of elbow joint

occasional.notes: Due to disuse or nerve involvement
Rarely, nerve compression may occur near the pseudoarthrosis

rare.notes: Pathological fracture due to bone weakness
Due to chronic deformity and disuse

imaging: X-ray showing nonunion or pseudoarthrosis of the ulna with bone sclerosis and deformity
MRI may show fibrous tissue at pseudoarthrosis site
CT scan for detailed bone architecture assessment
genetic: Possible association with NF1 gene mutations if neurofibromatosis type 1 is present
other: Clinical examination revealing abnormal mobility and deformity of the ulna

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement of the radius instead of the ulna
Different deformity pattern and clinical presentation
History of trauma or fracture preceding nonunion
Absence of congenital deformity at birth
Generalized bone fragility with multiple fractures
Blue sclerae and other systemic features

redFlags: Development of neurological deficits in the affected limb
Signs of infection or inflammation at the pseudoarthrosis site
references: Orphanet: Congenital pseudoarthrosis of the ulna - ORPHA:295026
